title: A nature said to last a lifetime
odia:
ଘୁଷୁରି ପ୍ରକୃତି ପଙ୍କେ ଲୋଟେ
ମଣିଷ ପ୍ରକୃତି ମଲେ ତୁଟେ।
literal_meaning: A pig’s nature is to wallow in mud; a person’s nature ends only at death.
meaning_odia: ଘୁଷୁରିର ପଙ୍କରେ ଲୋଟିବା ସହ ମଣିଷର ପ୍ରକୃତିକୁ ମିଳାଇ ବକ୍ତା କହୁଛନ୍ତି ଯେ ତାହା ମୃତ୍ୟୁବେଳେ ହିଁ ତୁଟେ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ବାରମ୍ବାର ଫେରିଆସୁଥିବା ଅଭ୍ୟାସ ବା ସ୍ୱଭାବ ପ୍ରତି ଏହା ଏକ କଠୋର ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ; ମଣିଷର ବଦଳିବାର କ୍ଷମତା ବିଷୟରେ ପ୍ରମାଣ ନୁହେଁ।
explanation: The first line supplies a repeated behaviour; the second turns persistence into an absolute claim lasting until death. Read editorially, the saying expresses frustration or certainty about an entrenched disposition. Its force comes from that exaggeration, rather than establishing that a person cannot change.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A colleague returns to the same habit after repeatedly promising to alter it. Someone quotes the saying in frustration at the recurrence. This illustrates the speaker’s judgment, not a settled prediction about the colleague.
cultural_context: ପ୍ରକୃତି links the animal and human lines, while ଲୋଟେ and ତୁଟେ bind them in rhyme. Mud gives the first line a visible action; death gives the second its emphatic endpoint.

odia_summary: ପୁଣି ଫେରିଆସୁଥିବା ସ୍ୱଭାବକୁ ଆଜୀବନ ରହିବା ବୋଲି ବକ୍ତା ଟିପ୍ପଣୀ କରନ୍ତି।
english_summary: The speaker pictures an entrenched disposition as lasting a lifetime.
